body.text: Before this record was opened, in the same chat on 2026-11-19 (17:48-17:57 UTC), the agent ran five unrecorded web searches (AI auto arranger software; automatic arrangement MIDI plugins; Band-in-a-Box 2026; MusicXML automatic arrangement for chosen instruments; Sibelius Arrange feature) and told the supervisor it found no commercial product that takes a MusicXML score and arranges it live for chosen instruments. Products seen then: Band-in-a-Box, RapidComposer, JMT Orchestrator, BackupBand, Texturium, Orb Composer, LANDR Composer, InstaComposer, Muse, ShevtoneAudio, Sibelius Arrange, Dorico Explode, Klangio, Songscription, AiHud Notation Copilot, and research systems (NeurIPS 2025 unified arrangement model; CMMR 2023 monophonic MusicXML arranger). That exploration suggested hypothesis H1 and is not evidence for it.

As of November 2026, which software products, online services and research systems can automatically or semi-automatically arrange existing music into a notated score that musicians read, for a set of instruments the user chooses; and for each, what input it takes, what notation it outputs, whether it uses machine learning or rules, and whether it works interactively or in real time?

body.definition: A software product, online service or research system that, from existing musical material (a melody, chords, a score or a performance), automatically or semi-automatically produces parts for instruments: by orchestrating, harmonising, voicing, exploding or reducing. The unit of analysis: one system, counted once across versions and editions.

The system delivers its arrangement as notation a musician reads: a score or parts in standard staff notation, exported as MusicXML, PDF or a notation application's file, or written into a notation editor.

code.include: The system's own description or documentation shows the arrangement as staff notation, or exports MusicXML, PDF score/parts, or a notation-app file.
code.exclude: Output only as audio, MIDI without notation, tablature or chord charts alone, or piano-roll.

body.definition: The user selects the instruments or ensemble the arrangement is written for.

code.include: The user picks target instruments, an ensemble, or a template of instruments, and the parts are written for that choice.
code.exclude: A fixed instrumentation (e.g. piano only, or a style's fixed band) the user cannot change instrument by instrument.

body.definition: The system accepts notated music as its input.

code.include: Accepts MusicXML, or works on a score inside a notation application (which reads MusicXML).
code.exclude: Accepts only audio, MIDI, chord symbols, text prompts or live playing.

body.definition: The arrangement is produced by a model trained on data (machine learning, neural network, LLM).

code.include: The developer states that a trained model (machine learning, neural network, deep learning, LLM, 'AI model') generates the arrangement.
code.exclude: 'AI' used as a label without saying that a trained model produces the arrangement; such systems are coded unclear method.

body.definition: The arrangement is produced by hand-written rules, styles, templates or algorithms without a trained model.

code.include: The developer describes style files, templates, rules, voice-leading algorithms or search procedures, or an independent review does.
code.exclude: Any trained model generating the arrangement.

body.definition: The sources do not say whether a trained model or rules produce the arrangement.

code.include: Marketed as 'AI' or 'intelligent' with no statement of how the arrangement is produced.
code.exclude: Either ML method or rules method applies.

body.definition: The arrangement is regenerated in response to the user's choices or playing without an offline export-import cycle.

code.include: Arrangement updates live as the user plays, changes instruments or settings, within the same session.
code.exclude: A one-off batch generation the user must re-run from scratch.

body.definition: Sold or licensed to the public (paid, subscription or freemium) at the date of retrieval.

code.include: A price, subscription or purchase page exists at retrieval.
code.exclude: Free open-source, free-only, discontinued, or research-only systems.

body.definition: Available to the public at no cost at retrieval.

code.include: Free download or free web use, or published code.
code.exclude: Paid-only or research descriptions without public access.

body.definition: Described in a research publication (paper, preprint, thesis) rather than offered as a product.

code.include: The source is a paper, preprint or thesis describing the system.
code.exclude: A product whose maker also published a paper is coded by its availability as a product.

body.definition: A commercially available arranging system, not made by Syntonic Labs, that takes score input and uses an ML method to produce notated output for a user-chosen instrumentation.

code.include: The same system is coded commercially available, score input, ML method, notated output and user-chosen instrumentation.
code.exclude: Any of the five missing, or the system is a Syntonic Labs product (Tempered).

body.definition: A fixed set of web searches run on one or two days, each result screened against the inclusion criteria, with one level of snowballing from included roundups, then each included system coded by a fixed codebook (summative content analysis, deductive).
